title: Inbound Pay-Per-Call & RTB Ping-Post Arbitrage — Practitioner Testimony Operator Workbook
subtitle: A field workbook for modeling call margins, wiring RTB ring trees, building IVR qualification gates, controlling routing and attribution, running ping-post auctions, and capturing one-to-one consent before a single paid call goes live

worksheets.title: Call Economics and Platform Readiness Ledger
worksheets.purpose: Turn the pay-per-call model into hard numbers before any spend: choose a starting lane, prove the spread survives a weak paid ratio, own the tracking layer, and wire an RTB ring tree with revenue floors, timeouts, latency buffers, paused buyers, and tested failover.
instructions: Fill every field with numbers from a real offer you are evaluating, never placeholder figures or averages you cannot defend.
Complete the spread model and paid-ratio stress test before touching platform settings, because the margin decides every routing choice downstream.
Read the full offer page and copy its rules verbatim, including minimum call length, buyer hours, hold period, and buyer ownership.
Build the ring tree, timeouts, and buffers inside your own tracking account, keeping every new buyer paused until each is ready.
Place live test calls and log every result; any failed check sends you back to the matching field before spend.

fields.name: lane_selection
fields.prompt: State the starting lane you will run first: pay-per-call through a network, pay-per-lead, a hybrid funnel, or direct local clients. Explain why that lane fits your current budget, approval odds, and tolerance for slow-paying businesses right now.
fields.example: Starting on network pay-per-call for easy approval, accepting thinner checks. Matt Wacek warns that nine times out of 10 an affiliate network pays its bill while a business sometimes does not [Matt Wacek — uxYMcIUwpLA @ 00:06:30]. A hybrid lead-form backup stays ready, pushing urgency on the thank-you page where some Leadbase Pro members reach a 40% call rate [Leadbase — ewNftdwX784 @ 00:12:52].

fields.name: spread_model
fields.prompt: Write the per-call revenue, publisher payout, and margin for your first offer. Show the arithmetic line by line, name who keeps the spread, and note whether a direct buyer-seller deal would leave any margin to split at all.
fields.example: Revenue $50, publisher payout $35, network margin $15 per qualified call, mirroring the TrackDrive split [TrackDrive — V1FTIO7peWA @ 00:02:27]. If selling direct, there is no middle margin, so the full $50 lands with the publisher. Brokered roofing calls follow ceohec's 40% minimum markup, buying at $150 and reselling at $210 [ceohec — Rcc1hu6P28g @ 00:04:34].

fields.name: paid_ratio_stress_test
fields.prompt: Model the worst-case paid ratio for your offer. Assume the buyer pays for only a fraction of delivered calls, then recalculate your true cost per paid call and decide the lowest ratio at which the campaign still clears profit.
fields.example: Leadbase saw debt buyers receive 10 calls and agree to pay for three [Leadbase — ewNftdwX784 @ 00:06:44]. At a $50 generation cost, paying on three of ten pushes true cost to $150 per paid call [Leadbase — ewNftdwX784 @ 00:06:55]. Floor set at five of ten paid; below that, traffic pauses and the buyer gets renegotiated or replaced.

fields.name: offer_page_audit
fields.prompt: Copy every rule from the offer page before you build anything: minimum call length, buyer hours, hold period, geography, and who owns the buyer relationship. Flag any rule that conflicts with your traffic source or planned call hours.
fields.example: Offer page read line by line per WordsAtScale: minimum call length, buyer hours, hold period, and buyer ownership all logged [WordsAtScale — DJFaYJ3O7aU @ 00:01:59]. A call that meets those rules is qualified and gets paid; one that misses is not [TrackDrive — _h1_mcKPGjY @ 00:08:23]. Conflict flagged: buyer closes at 6 p.m. while ads run until 9 p.m.

fields.name: own_tracking_layer
fields.prompt: Name the tracking number you will place in front of the network's number and the platform that issues it. Describe how you will verify every call, catch skimming, and compare your counts against the network's reported qualified calls.
fields.example: A Ringba number sits in front of the network number on every placement, so each call is logged before handoff [Ringba — 4kaOQgGnpJo @ 00:13:58]. Ringba stresses using your own call tracking [Ringba — 4kaOQgGnpJo @ 00:07:21]. Weekly, own counts get compared against network-reported qualified calls, and any gap over a few calls triggers a dispute.

fields.name: compliance_creative_check
fields.prompt: List every ad, sign, or page that will generate calls and mark any claim that could mislead a caller. Record how consent will be captured and stored, given that a litigator suing your client can pull you in too.
fields.example: Three ad creatives reviewed; one promising a guaranteed settlement was dropped as misleading, following John Casto's warning that a litigator suing the client puts the publisher on the hook too [John Casto — XQvPekJ-K8M @ 00:03:23]. Consent records are captured on the landing page with timestamp and stored per caller. Casto would rather sell 100 calls than 1,000 leads.

fields.name: rtb_buyer_stack
fields.prompt: Map your routing plan for one campaign: which buyers sit in the ring tree as dynamic RTB targets, which sit underneath as static fallbacks, the minimum revenue floor, and what happens when no bid clears that floor.
fields.example: Ring tree with three dynamic targets and a $29.01 minimum revenue floor; if no bid beats 29, routing falls to the next static target or another ring tree [Ringba — WOqDYpchQOo @ 00:04:11]. Ringba estimates earnings per call from past buyer behavior to pick the winner [Ringba — yat7hRHHsKY @ 00:08:04]. Two static buyers sit underneath as catch-all failover.

fields.name: timeout_and_buffer_settings
fields.prompt: Record the exact dial timeout, ping timeout, buyer billable buffer, and publisher billable duration for this campaign. Show the latency pad you added so connect and ring time never leave you paying for a call your buyer rejected.
fields.example: Dial timeout 10 seconds and ping timeout 3,000 milliseconds, matching the RingbaX seller ring tree recipe [Ringba — uDzWrD17wqg @ 00:02:04]. Buyer buffer 120 seconds; publisher pitched at 128 seconds using ceohec's 8-second latency pad [ceohec — RWVdTqjVYE8 @ 00:09:59]. Conversion propagation switched on for Retreaver-to-Retreaver routes so both sides agree [ceohec — RWVdTqjVYE8 @ 00:06:05].

fields.name: buyer_onboarding_controls
fields.prompt: Describe how each new buyer enters a live campaign without receiving calls early. Note whether the buyer is paused on entry, which fields hide publisher names and IDs, and whether the buyer accepts SIP delivery for faster connections.
fields.example: New buyer added with pause buyer hit first, since buyers go live immediately on entry [ceohec — RWVdTqjVYE8 @ 00:15:37]. Publisher names and IDs stay out of collaborator-visible fields [ceohec — RWVdTqjVYE8 @ 00:07:05]. Buyer accepts SIP, so routing uses it for faster connection, better voice quality, and header data [Ringba — BOFMLupLrSM @ 00:03:59].

fields.name: end_to_end_test_log
fields.prompt: Log the real test calls you placed before sending paid traffic. For each, confirm tracking fired, the correct buyer received it, someone answered, the duration timed correctly, and the recording saved, then note any failure and its fix.
fields.example: Five test calls placed before any paid spend, checking tracking, buyer routing, answer, timing, and recording end to end [TrackDrive — ncatAE6wf_0 @ 00:02:38]. Call three hit voicemail because buyer hours were wrong; fixed and retested. Every call recorded, echoing the case where Ringba recordings captured every call a business received [Ringba — RVobRCTpSEg @ 00:03:51].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not send paid traffic until the spread math survives a three-of-ten paid ratio, your own tracking number sits in front of every network number, the ring tree carries a revenue floor with static fallbacks underneath, publisher durations include the 8-second pad, and five live test calls pass end to end.

worksheets.title: IVR Qualification Gates and Routing Control Map
worksheets.purpose: Design IVR gates that sort callers on the attribute that decides payout, then control everything after qualification: number pools, tag filters fed by URL parameters, priority and weight tiers, dollar caps, duplicate remonetization, zip-level geo routing, and recording reviews that expose weak buyers.
instructions: Start with the single attribute your buyer pays on, then build every menu and filter around protecting it.
Script each IVR prompt word for word, keeping menus short and placing a hang-up node on every failure path.
Map every quiz answer to a URL parameter and a matching tag filter before connecting any target.
Set priority, weight, concurrency, dollar caps, and hours for each buyer, treating unverified capacity claims as warnings.
Listen to a sample of recordings weekly and rewrite routing whenever agents, buyer IVRs, or hours burn revenue.

fields.name: payout_attribute
fields.prompt: Name the single caller attribute that decides payout on this campaign, such as debt level, insurance status, or homeownership. Write the exact IVR question, the key that qualifies, and the key that disqualifies the caller before any buyer phone rings.
fields.example: Attribute: unsecured credit card debt. Prompt asks whether the caller has more than $10,000; press 1 means qualified and forwarded, press 2 means not qualified [Ringba — 4dnXkZ7u6zw @ 00:00:51]. Only the press-1 caller reaches the buyer and earns affiliate credit. A press-key robocall check sits in front, terminating callers who cannot complete it [Ringba — Ua5XxaPrhRs @ 00:04:54].

fields.name: reask_and_failure_path
fields.prompt: Design the path for callers who answer wrong, time out, or press an unknown key. State how many retries they get, what audio cue loops them back, and where the hang-up node sits on the failed-connection branch.
fields.example: Callers claiming coverage on the ACA flow get re-asked, because many press the wrong key the first time, per Carlos Corona. An attempt variable increments on each gather failure; after two failed attempts the call disconnects [SignalWire — VByuomL6T0s @ 00:04:54]. A hang-up node closes the failed-connection path so the tree validates and saves [Ringba — Vd_ZoE2BRqQ @ 00:02:22].

fields.name: non_qualified_monetization
fields.prompt: Decide what happens to callers who fail the screen. Choose between hanging up, routing to an adjacent buyer, or converting them into an SMS opt-in, and list the data fields your opt-in webhook will carry downstream.
fields.example: Failed-screen Medicare callers from an ACA ad are not dumped on Medicare buyers; Corona says that works for days or weeks before complaints arrive [Carlos Corona — tf4AieS7Mhc @ 00:03:55]. Instead they convert into an IVR SMS opt-in, with the webhook carrying call UUID, E.164 number, campaign, and state for later follow-up.

fields.name: menu_and_voice_design
fields.prompt: Write your menu options in order and count them. Note which options are most common and listed first, whether prompts switch voices to hold attention, and whether any step should run silently in the background instead.
fields.example: Four options, most common first, staying under the five-option ceiling [GetVoIP - Simplify your search — 7vsOEhARsdU @ 00:02:23]. Prompts alternate between two voices because Corona found callers pay more attention when the voice changes [Carlos Corona — tf4AieS7Mhc @ 00:07:06]. Buyer menus are skipped with Dial IVR sending DTMF tones in the background [Ringba — VQKxVnPn5zE @ 00:00:15].

fields.name: quiz_parameter_passing
fields.prompt: List each quiz or landing-page answer you will pass into the call platform as a URL parameter or tag. For each, name the router filter it feeds and the buyer condition it enforces, such as carrier or homeowner status.
fields.example: Auto insurance quiz passes carrier and homeowner answers into Ringba URL parameters, so two exclusive buyers are filtered on whether the visitor owns a home [Landerlab — DMS29IlU8pE @ 00:16:17]. Each answer becomes a tag routing filter at the target level, making a target eligible only when the call meets its conditions [Ringba — 4MDNmxviCKk @ 00:00:36].

fields.name: number_pool_verification
fields.prompt: Describe how you confirmed the dynamic number pool is working on the live landing page. Record the base number, the swapped number you saw, the mobile test call you placed, and the tag that appeared in the call log.
fields.example: Preview showed the base number replaced, confirming the Ringba number pool script loaded; a live mobile test then showed the carrier tag in the call log [Landerlab — DMS29IlU8pE @ 00:10:33]. The pool locks one number to each browser session until the visitor goes idle, closes the browser, or leaves the page [Ringba — pNWCpdBjuPA @ 00:00:35].

fields.name: ai_webhook_fallback
fields.prompt: If an AI voice agent answers any inbound calls, document the webhook router's response time, retry behavior, and default fallback agent. Confirm each dynamic variable name matches exactly between the webhook response and the agent prompt.
fields.example: Retell inbound webhook must answer inside 10 seconds; it retries up to three times, then falls back to the default agent on the number [Henryk Brzozowski — p7WavoW_6to @ 00:04:24]. The caller_name variable is spelled identically in the make.com response and the agent prompt, otherwise the name will not populate [Henryk Brzozowski — p7WavoW_6to @ 00:07:13].

fields.name: priority_weight_caps
fields.prompt: Lay out every target's priority tier, weight, concurrency cap, dollar cap, and hours of operation including lunch breaks. Mark which buyers are new, the hard dollar exposure each carries until their first payment clears, and any quoted hours not yet verified.
fields.example: Priority one holds two direct buyers split by weight; if neither is available, priority two takes the call [Ringba — 0eCCbtHmCJE @ 00:02:15]. The new buyer is capped at $2,000 for the first two weeks until payment lands [Ringba — yFkULiyenzk @ 00:01:44]. One network quotes 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.; recordings get checked for later answering [Ringba — ojcbZuG798w @ 00:50:23].

fields.name: duplicate_and_geo_routing
fields.prompt: Explain how duplicate callers and geography will be handled. State your duplicate rule, where repeat callers route for remonetization, and whether geo routing uses area code or a more precise location signal such as zip, and the duplicate share you expect.
fields.example: Budgeting duplicates at 5% to 25% of call flow, per Ringba platform statistics [Ringba — ojcbZuG798w @ 00:14:05]. Repeat callers route to a second network instead of being dropped. Geo routing uses zip, not area code, since roughly 35% of people live outside their area code [Ringba — ojcbZuG798w @ 00:22:10]. Zip-level routing lifted one mortgage client from $10 to $250 per call.

fields.name: concurrency_and_recording_review
fields.prompt: Record each buyer's stated concurrency and how you verified it. Then summarize what your call recordings revealed about back-end agents, buyer IVRs, and greetings, and list the buyers you will pause, renegotiate, or replace as a result.
fields.example: Network claimed unlimited concurrency; flagged, since ten extra CC is reasonable while 500 into one giant buyer is fishy [Ringba — ojcbZuG798w @ 00:55:36]. Recordings exposed a back-end buyer with weak agents and a long IVR burning return on investment [Ringba — ojcbZuG798w @ 00:48:43]. That buyer now gets auto-dialed IVR selections or gets replaced [Ringba — ojcbZuG798w @ 00:47:46].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not route live traffic until the IVR validates with a hang-up node on every failure path, non-qualified callers have a defined destination other than a mismatched buyer, the number pool swap and carrier tag are confirmed on a mobile test, every new buyer carries a hard dollar cap, and duplicates route to a second buyer.

worksheets.title: Ping-Post Auction Rules and One-to-One Consent Audit
worksheets.purpose: Run ping-post lead and call auctions on defensible rules, then prove every contact rests on one-to-one consent: margin carves, timeout windows, refund caps, fallback scenarios, call campaign safeguards, earnings-per-call checks, consent wording, consent records, and source rejection criteria.
instructions: Write the auction rules before onboarding any buyer, including margin, timeouts, refund cap, and matching priority.
Start every dynamic source on plain Yes and change fallback settings only after the math proves a gain.
Enter call durations in the unit the platform expects and launch on one small geo with a low cap.
Copy consent language exactly as consumers see it, and attach a sample consent record to each buyer file.
Reject any source that cannot produce documented, company-specific consent, regardless of volume or price offered.

fields.name: ping_post_flow
fields.prompt: Describe your ping-post sequence from first ping to final post. Identify which buyers receive the non-contact ping, which filters exclude them, when PII is released, and what the seller sees if no buyer responds inside the timeout window.
fields.example: Non-contact ping fires simultaneously to every buyer with an active account, funds, and a matching filter set; the PII post lands only after the buyer returns success. Extra fields often trigger exclusion [boberdoo.com — vNu0tV99Lnw @ 00:07:35]. If no response returns in 20 seconds, the seller gets a generic unmatched [boberdoo.com — YLw0lKsOayk @ 00:09:51].

fields.name: margin_carve
fields.prompt: Write the margin you carve off each buyer bid before the offer returns to the seller. State whether it is a fixed dollar amount or a percentage tier, and show the resulting offer for at least two sample bids.
fields.example: Fixed $2 margin: a $10 bid returns an $8 offer to the seller, and a $3 margin drops it to $7 [boberdoo.com — yCAVYNpSdZI @ 00:28:04]. The vendor then decides whether to accept the $8 offer and send the post [boberdoo.com — lpWTQpnduYo @ 00:05:43]. Larger accounts move to variable tiers between 10% and 50%.

fields.name: timeout_windows
fields.prompt: Set the ping timeout and post timeout for every source, and explain how lagging buyers will be excluded so the seller always receives a bid back. Note any source that requires longer windows and the reason it was granted.
fields.example: Standard sources run 15 seconds on the ping and 30 on the post, with lagging buyers excluded so the seller always gets a bid back [boberdoo.com — yCAVYNpSdZI @ 00:15:39]. One aggregator source runs 20 seconds on the ping and 60 on the post because its buyer API returns slowly during peak hours.

fields.name: refund_and_priority_rules
fields.prompt: Record the refund cap on every buyer account, the window it covers, and each buyer's matching priority. Explain how buyers sharing a priority are rotated and how you will stop any single buyer from refunding most of what they receive.
fields.example: Refund cap set at 15% of leads over 30 days on every buyer, installed before onboarding, so no buyer can refund 90 of 100 [boberdoo.com — yCAVYNpSdZI @ 00:22:50]. All buyers default to matching priority five and rotate round robin [boberdoo.com — I3MdV-IDLRk @ 00:24:08]. The highest-paying direct buyer moves up one priority level.

fields.name: fallback_and_scenarios
fields.prompt: State whether each dynamic source starts on plain Yes or on yes but sold non-exclusively, and whether you run exclusive or shared scenarios. Show the math proving any non-exclusive or shared sale beats selling the lead once.
fields.example: Every dynamic source starts on Yes; the non-exclusive fallback stays off because it can sell a lead at a loss [boberdoo.com — EKrBDZYFq2A @ 00:23:24]. Scenarios compare one exclusive $20 sale against two shared sales: selling it twice at $12 makes 24 compared to 20 [boberdoo.com — W03nRhCi63A @ 00:31:46]. Shared wins only when two buyers clear $10.

fields.name: call_campaign_setup
fields.prompt: Document your ping-post call campaign settings: number type ordered, duration field units, starting geo, and daily cap. Explain how many days you will hold the campaign small and how you will hide the number when no buyer is available.
fields.example: Local numbers ordered for lower monthly and per-minute cost [boberdoo.com — CSGuZ-Sping @ 00:06:49]. Duration entered as 2 minutes, not 120, after clients created 120-minute durations [boberdoo.com — CSGuZ-Sping @ 00:17:10]. One metro, low daily cap, held for several days. JavaScript number display hides the phone at 1 a.m. when no buyer is open [boberdoo.com — I3MdV-IDLRk @ 00:12:24].

fields.name: epc_vs_bid_check
fields.prompt: Compare your highest-bidding call buyer against your best earnings-per-call buyer. Record each buyer's bid, duration requirement, and actual paid rate, then decide which buyer should win routing priority on earnings rather than headline price for the next test cycle.
fields.example: Buyer A bids $50 with a duration gate; Buyer B bids $30 with no duration requirement. The call desk warns the $50 buyer can lose on earnings per call to the $30 buyer. Calldrive routes to the highest earnings per call, and lower bids simply mean fewer calls [Calldrive — jHMaZ1k0rpY @ 00:06:16]. Buyer B wins priority this cycle.

fields.name: consent_language
fields.prompt: Paste the consent language from your form exactly as a consumer sees it. Confirm it names one business per unchecked box, has no select-all or pre-check, matches the ad's context, and lists every regulated technology you might use.
fields.example: Form shows 15 checkboxes for 15 buyers under an individual bid scenario [ActiveProspect, Inc. — uXTg2yB_ZTM @ 00:44:12]. Single select for each item, no select all, and no pre-check [TechMarketer — B9lfPgUUls0 @ 00:00:43]. The call to action changed from select the best to compare after single picks dominated [ActiveProspect, Inc. — uXTg2yB_ZTM @ 00:22:42].

fields.name: consent_record_proof
fields.prompt: Describe the consent record each buyer receives before any outbound contact. List the token, IP address, session video, timestamp, and checked company name it contains, and confirm the buyer physically holds that record before dialing or texting.
fields.example: Each record carries a consent token, the IP address, and a video of the form fill, mirroring Calldrive's capture [Calldrive — jHMaZ1k0rpY @ 00:02:28]. The buyer takes physical possession of the record before calling, with the consumer having checked a box naming that exact company [Evocalize — h8PlsMHs16k @ 00:01:27]. Buyers need one-to-one consent as well [ActiveProspect, Inc. — uXTg2yB_ZTM @ 00:47:31].

fields.name: source_rejection_and_exposure
fields.prompt: List every lead or call source under review and the reason each passes or fails. Note vague or blanket consent, missing documentation, or high volume with thin verification, and write the per-violation fine range you are budgeting against.
fields.example: Source two rejected for blanket our-partners consent and no documentation [Pitchit — k6g6hxICGH4 @ 00:07:03]. Troutman estimates only two of 10 circulating one-to-one forms pass [Seasalt AI — KBFaRW7QmVQ @ 00:33:10]. Exposure budgeted at $500 to $2,000 per text or call [Seasalt AI — KBFaRW7QmVQ @ 00:14:15]. Rule status is contested, so the form stays compliant regardless.

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not accept a ping or dial a lead until the margin carve, timeout windows, and 15% refund cap are configured, every dynamic source starts on plain Yes, call durations are verified in minutes, and every buyer holds a consent record naming their exact company.

worksheets.title: Traffic Engine: Google, Meta, and Home-Services Call Verticals
worksheets.purpose: Build a paid traffic plan that treats the billable call as the only scoreboard, pairing search intent on Google and cheaper volume on Meta with an emergency home-services vertical whose payouts, buffers, and seasonality leave a real spread after ad cost.
instructions: Write down the payout and billable buffer of your chosen offer before you estimate any channel cost, so every number below is measured against what a call actually earns.
Plan Google builds around Search campaigns with call assets, since new call-only ads are blocked from February 2026, and keep Performance Max and Smart out of the account.
Treat Meta as cheaper but riskier volume, and record the billable rate you need rather than celebrating a low cost per raw call.
Pull payout data by zip, day, and hour before choosing geography, and read every network's fine print before writing a single line of ad copy.
Do not move to the next worksheet until a controlled spend has proven billable percentage, revenue per call, and return on spend with more than one buyer lined up.

fields.name: channel_cost_benchmark
fields.prompt: List each traffic channel you plan to test and write the cost per call you expect from it, then state the payout your offer pays so you can see whether the spread survives before a single dollar of media is spent.
fields.example: Ventura's ranges set the plan: Google at $50-150 per call, Facebook and Instagram at $15-40, and YouTube, TikTok and Outbrain at $25-60, with Meta creative refreshed every 2-3 weeks to hold the low end [John Ventura — GV0ML_xytX8 @ 00:04:04]. Against a $42 pest payout, only the Meta range leaves room for profit.

fields.name: google_campaign_structure
fields.prompt: Describe how your Google build will work now that new call-only ads are blocked: campaign type, ad format, device bid adjustments, landing page behavior, and the call length you will count as a conversion inside the account before launch.
fields.example: Downey Marketing flagged new call-only ads disappear in February 2026 [Downey Marketing — 4jiwxMObZvQ @ 00:01:07], so the build is a plain Search campaign with responsive search ads plus call assets, desktop and tablet bids at minus 100 percent, a tap-to-call mobile page, and any call over 15 seconds counted as a conversion [Hasib Ashad - Google Ads — Y4oieZQ07T8 @ 00:03:55].

fields.name: negative_keyword_loop
fields.prompt: Explain the routine you will run to keep irrelevant searches from producing paid calls, including where your starting negative list comes from, how often you review call recordings, and who adds new terms to the account each week.
fields.example: Day one starts with the network's own negative list instead of a blank sheet [Dollar_Earn_with_us — e4KqhdonStw @ 00:34:52]. Every morning the team listens to yesterday's recordings and pushes each irrelevant request into negatives [Ringba — YhBQnt2AHbI @ 00:00:59]. Caller wording that does convert gets fed back into ad copy [Sabri Suby — u57s5wmdl5s @ 00:16:49].

fields.name: meta_call_flow
fields.prompt: Choose the Meta format you will run for calls, whether call-now buttons, Reach campaigns, or a lead-to-call flow, and write the cost per call, cost per billable call, and billable rate you must hit to stay profitable on that platform.
fields.example: Health insurance on Facebook is benchmarked at $8-15 per call, $20-25 per billable call and a 40-70 percent billable rate, with CPM near $10 and CTR at 1-1.5 percent [Marketcall — 9msaK2zlGMI @ 00:29:13]. The campaign caps bids at five to eight dollars per call click with a one-day conversion window [Marketcall — 9msaK2zlGMI @ 00:22:40].

fields.name: answer_speed_failover
fields.prompt: Write down the maximum seconds a caller may ring before a human answers, the failover that fires when nobody picks up, and the follow-up step that rescues callers who refuse to leave a voicemail on your line during buyer hours.
fields.example: Answer inside 30 seconds, because pickup in that window converts at 31 percent while answering after five minutes drops to 4 percent and 80 percent of callers will not leave a voicemail [John Ventura — GV0ML_xytX8 @ 00:07:43]. If nobody answers in 10-15 seconds, an auto-SMS fires and a five-minute callback is scheduled for the caller.

fields.name: vertical_selection
fields.prompt: Name the home-services vertical you will enter first and justify it with emergency intent, payout range, billable buffer, and seasonality, then list the single urgent service you will sell as the foot in the door with local buyers.
fields.example: Pest control first: offer 11558 pays $20-$65 per call on a 90-125 second buffer, set by zip [Marketcall — g3sxn6A6bDc @ 00:03:56]. Testing begins in early April so campaigns are dialed in before the May-September peak, when volume rises 40-60 percent [Marketcall — g3sxn6A6bDc @ 00:06:09]. Google autocomplete 'emergency' searches confirm urgency [Ryan Moran — yB7cDGVlP0k @ 00:00:47].

fields.name: geo_bid_map
fields.prompt: Record the payout threshold you will use to build your geographic target list, the tool or export you will pull it from, and how you will check whether payouts shift by day of week or hour of the day before setting bids.
fields.example: Filter the Bid Map for zips paying over $50, check payouts by day and by hour, and export the result to Excel as the geo-target list [Marketcall — g3sxn6A6bDc @ 00:04:36]. Against a $42 average payout and $20-$28 average ad cost, profit lands near $10-$20 per call [Marketcall — g3sxn6A6bDc @ 00:06:41], so low-paying zips stay excluded.

fields.name: low_cost_source_test
fields.prompt: Describe one low-cost call source you will test outside of paid search, such as classifieds or physical signage, including the cost per placement, the payout trigger, the tracking method, and the return you need to keep it running each month.
fields.example: A Craigslist-only plumbing offer pays $16 on any call over 90 seconds; each Hennepin County small business post costs $5, so one qualified lead returns 4x [Matt Wacek — S1xXLvaXSvU @ 00:05:02]. Posts run plain text, no images, with the phone number repeated several times [Matt Wacek — S1xXLvaXSvU @ 00:07:11], each on its own tracked number.

fields.name: network_fine_print
fields.prompt: List the creative rules and restrictions from each network's offer page that will shape your ad copy, including banned phrases, required phrases, and naming rules, and note how your business name will match your ad domain before writing a headline.
fields.example: Network A bans the phrase 'free estimate' while Network B requires it, so copy is written only after both fine-print pages are read line by line [Matt Wacek — S1xXLvaXSvU @ 00:01:14]. The Google business name is set to match the domain the ads point to [Marketcall — 9msaK2zlGMI @ 01:04:47], and a dedicated vertical page replaces any general landing page.

fields.name: controlled_spend_gate
fields.prompt: Set the controlled test budget, the billable percentage, revenue per call, and return on spend you must prove before scaling, and name the backup buyers you have lined up so one account never becomes a single point of failure.
fields.example: Billable percentage, revenue per call and ROI are proven on a controlled spend before pushing toward $10,000, never judged on raw call count [ExclusiveLiveCall — grygjesM2j8 @ 00:09:30]. Brokering starts at a $3-5 margin, where 50 calls a day at $10 margin yields $500 daily [Nate Ancelet — q4tpqSo7KCE @ 00:10:09], with more than one buyer ready [Nate Ancelet — q4tpqSo7KCE @ 00:10:40].

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 4 is complete only when a controlled spend has proven billable percentage, revenue per call, and return on spend against your offer payout, an answer path under 30 seconds with a 10-15 second failover is live, network fine print has been checked against your copy, and more than one buyer is confirmed for every geography you target.

worksheets.title: Buyer-Side Discipline: Insurance Inbounds, Live Transfers, and Litigation Exposure
worksheets.purpose: Protect revenue per call on the buyer side by mapping billable buffers, scripting agents to hold price until qualification clears, covering every hour with enough buyers, and quantifying the TCPA and mass tort exposure that a single bad lead source can create.
instructions: Start with the billable buffer for every campaign, because a price quoted inside the buffer makes the call billable and disputes past the buffer are usually denied.
Write agent scripts that open with a question, hold price for at least 90 seconds, and qualify area, health, bank account, and age early.
Audit routing and buyer coverage before raising spend, since poor routing rather than creative is the most expensive mistake on inbound programs.
Run every purchased lead or transfer feed through consent, DNC, and reassigned-number checks before anyone dials it.
Model worst-case litigation exposure in dollars per call so the cost of one bad vendor is visible before you sign with them.

fields.name: billable_buffer_map
fields.prompt: List every campaign you will buy or sell into, with the exact billable buffer in seconds for each, and explain how your agents will know which buffer applies the moment a call connects to their line, and what happens if they guess wrong.
fields.example: The buffer sheet mirrors PRiMe Calls training: 20 seconds on FE raw inbound, 180 seconds on FE inbound transfer, 90 seconds on FE Spanish and FEX, and 60 seconds on CTV [PRiMeCalls — B5upgjqvbi4 @ 00:00:36]. The campaign name appears on the agent screen at connect, and quoting price inside a buffer makes the call billable [PRiMeCalls — B5upgjqvbi4 @ 00:02:34].

fields.name: rpc_floor
fields.prompt: State the revenue-per-call floor your agents must hold, the running call count you will measure it over, and the share of calls each agent must carry past ninety seconds to avoid being paused or removed from the inbound program.
fields.example: RPC is tracked on a 50-call running total, and agents stay above the $5 to $8 floor by taking at least three of every ten calls past 90 seconds [FFL Success Zone | Integrity Connect Inbounds — N3imbfBa8rI @ 00:26:38]. The target is Adeline's $18 RPC at about 40 percent of calls [FFL Success Zone | Integrity Connect Inbounds — -YRrdoKG1xs @ 00:07:47].

fields.name: inbound_script_opener
fields.prompt: Write the first three lines your agent will say on an inbound call, the question that opens the conversation, the four qualifiers asked before any price, and the closing question that replaces a passive check-in like how does that sound.
fields.example: Open with a question, never quote price inside 90 seconds, and qualify area, health, bank account and age early. The close swaps 'how does that sound' for 'have you heard enough to be able to make a decision today', then asks Visa, Mastercard or American Express, the sequence Derek finished in 4.5 minutes [Cody Askins — lRuXMEO6hbI @ 00:19:22].

fields.name: live_transfer_test
fields.prompt: Design a short live transfer test: the number of transfers you will buy, the price per transfer, the test length, and the cost per sale that would justify continuing, then name who will personally close during the test.
fields.example: Mirror Willie Goldberg's two-week run: 49 transfers at $25 each produced 5 sales, about 1 in 10, for roughly $250-300 per sale, with Willie closing 3 of the 5 personally [Willie Goldberg — A4zDgHX2VWI @ 00:01:15]. Continue only if cost per sale stays comfortably under that band and issued premium covers it.

fields.name: buyer_coverage_audit
fields.prompt: Map how many buyers cover each state and hour you sell into, what catches calls when every buyer is busy or closed, and how those unanswered callers are monetized later without ever being resold as leads to other buyers.
fields.example: Corona's incomplete Google setup produced hundreds of missed calls, and poor routing, not creative, was the biggest mistake [Ryan Clogg — 7Q7WzSONnX4 @ 00:11:35]. High volume needs quite a few buyers, so Retell AI or Synthflow catches unanswered calls, captures consent, and monetizes later via call-back, SMS, email, or resale as a click [Ryan Clogg — 7Q7WzSONnX4 @ 00:13:10].

fields.name: recording_retention
fields.prompt: Specify the call recording system you will use, whether every inbound call is recorded in full, how long audio and records are stored, and who on your team can pull a recording when a buyer disputes a call.
fields.example: Every call is recorded in full and kept for six years, as audio for at least the first three [JustCall — DOcBtaUIjpE @ 00:00:15]. Consent records, including scanned wet-signature forms, stay on file four to five years to cover the four-year TCPA statute of limitations [Channel Automation — NlU2OB8OEBI @ 00:26:21]. The compliance lead pulls disputed recordings.

fields.name: purchased_lead_consent
fields.prompt: Describe the checks every purchased lead or transfer feed must pass before your team dials it, covering whose company the consent names, whether it matches the product, lead age, and whether the vendor can pay an indemnification claim.
fields.example: Reject any form that does not name the company, since generic consent like agreeing to calls about solar cannot be relied on [Channel Automation — NlU2OB8OEBI @ 00:15:13]. Never buy aged leads, which carry fraud and untracked opt-outs [Channel Automation — NlU2OB8OEBI @ 00:34:59], and confirm the vendor can actually pay indemnification [Henson Legal — 8-P7UvS--tE @ 00:29:51].

fields.name: dnc_reassigned_scrub
fields.prompt: Explain the scrub sequence each record runs through before outbound contact, including your internal do-not-call list, the reassigned number database, and how a revocation travels back out to every downstream sub-vendor you rely on within the revocation window.
fields.example: Each purchased lead hits the internal DNC first, because an opted-out consumer resurfacing through a third-party form does not reopen permission [Channel Automation — NlU2OB8OEBI @ 00:39:49]. Aged records then run against the reassigned number database, since 100,000 wrong-number messages at $500 each is $50 million [Channel Automation — NlU2OB8OEBI @ 00:34:45]. Sub-vendors are mapped [Troutman Amin, LLP — RtsC_jp9Y_U @ 00:14:04].

fields.name: tort_intake_horizon
fields.prompt: If you generate mass tort or motor vehicle accident calls, describe the intake criteria your law firm buyers use, the payout horizon they face, and how shrinking criteria could change the value of calls you already sold.
fields.example: Mass tort buyers wait three to seven years to get paid, if ever, and intake criteria can shrink midstream [The Lovely Law Firm — Uh9pQb_1l_I @ 00:00:32]. MVA leads command three and sometimes four figures against 18,720 average daily accidents [Peak ROI — MR5_DoylzPY @ 00:04:04], and car-wreck intakes also screen for other health issues.

fields.name: litigation_exposure_model
fields.prompt: Calculate your worst-case exposure if one bad lead source slips through, using the per-call statutory floor, regulator penalties, and the number of calls you place monthly, and note which regulatory reading of one-to-one consent you follow and why.
fields.example: Each invalid call carries a $500 floor and up to $166,000 in regulator penalties [Channel Automation — NlU2OB8OEBI @ 00:16:53], and one bad lead put a Federal Savings Bank in a $17 billion certified class [Troutman Amin, LLP — AyhsduniOPA @ 00:05:46]. Revenx reports one-to-one consent vacated in 2025, but other TCPA rules still apply [Revenx — iqEAeq8xyfY @ 00:00:00].

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 5 is complete only when every campaign has a documented billable buffer, agents hold an RPC floor measured on a 50-call running total, buyer coverage and a catch-all for unanswered calls exist for every hour you sell, and each purchased lead source has passed consent, DNC, reassigned-number, and indemnification checks with a dollar exposure model on file.

worksheets.title: Network Leverage and Unit Economics: Buyers, Publishers, Margin, and the Scale Gate
worksheets.purpose: Turn a single affiliate relationship into a load-balanced network that moves toward direct buyers, then lock the unit economics, payment terms, QA process, and scale thresholds that keep the spread intact as publishers and volume grow.
instructions: Apply to several networks at once and let side-by-side routing tests, not stated payouts, decide which buyers earn your traffic.
Collect conversion and capacity data in writing before negotiating, and never threaten a takeaway unless the backup route is already configured.
Write the full unit economics of one call, including rejects, duplicates, telecom cost, and buyer credit risk, before you quote any publisher a payout.
Collect buyer deposits upfront and align net terms so buyer money clears before publishers are paid.
Scale only when billable rate, post-reconciliation margin, and QA all clear the bar, and add affiliates in small steps rather than ten at once.

fields.name: network_application_plan
fields.prompt: List the pay-per-call networks you will apply to this month, the number of acceptances you expect, and the test that will reveal which network actually pays best once real calls start flowing through each one of them.
fields.example: Apply to 8-12 networks and expect 4-6 acceptances [Ryan Moran — NC4s18S7p00 @ 00:04:32]. One network may pay more but have an inaccurate zip list, so testing reveals the truth [Ryan Moran — NC4s18S7p00 @ 00:04:00]. In Ringba's capacity test, 50 calls each saw Network A pay 8 and Network B pay 19 [Ringba — 20s5iGyl_MY @ 00:52:19].

fields.name: concurrency_verification
fields.prompt: Record the guaranteed concurrency figure each network or buyer has confirmed in writing, how you will verify it against real traffic, and what your routing does with overflow calls that exceed that stated capacity during peak hours.
fields.example: Network B states a 100-per-day cap while Network A claims unlimited capacity, which is treated as a warning sign because dropped overflow is never refunded [Ringba — 20s5iGyl_MY @ 00:46:47]. Networks will not reimburse advertising costs when they lack capacity [Ringba — 20s5iGyl_MY @ 00:36:19], so overflow routes to a second network already configured.

fields.name: direct_buyer_path
fields.prompt: Describe how you will move from network buyers to direct buyers, including how you identify the real end buyer behind a network, how you reach them, and the price uplift you expect once the middle layer is removed.
fields.example: Call greetings reveal the real end buyer, who is then pitched directly [John Ventura — x3UYaJjRdx0 @ 00:05:57]. Competitors' ads get cold-called to reach their buyers, and outbound call centers get a pitch deck and an in-person visit [Ringba — AMwEMCOuhA0 @ 01:00:15]. Going direct is worth 100 to 300 points, turning a $10 call into $30-$80 [Ringba — RhODbxB4ylU @ 00:01:36].

fields.name: negotiation_leverage
fields.prompt: Write the data you will collect before asking a network for a payout bump, the exact comparison you will present, how the bump gets locked in writing, and the backup route that makes any takeaway threat real.
fields.example: Get the network's average conversion in chat before negotiating; a 20 versus 30 percent gap is pitched as '33% higher quality' and doubles as the case for going direct [Ringba — Jvd7AeYwbns @ 00:34:08]. The takeaway is threatened only with the backup route already configured, because a bluff kills future movement [Ringba — Jvd7AeYwbns @ 00:30:12].

fields.name: buyer_density
fields.prompt: Name the city or suburban market you will build in, count the buyers already active there, and explain how you will stack enough accounts so the whole business never hinges on one or two buyer relationships.
fields.example: A market qualifies only with at least 10 or 20 buyers, because with two the business is hinged on those two [Ringba — RhODbxB4ylU @ 00:25:51]. Payout alone does not decide placement: Network A pays $200 but monetizes 10 percent of traffic, while Network B pays $150 with broader coverage [ExclusiveLiveCall — Cu3vdN7Cn84 @ 00:03:45].

fields.name: duplicate_monetization
fields.prompt: Estimate the share of your call flow that arrives as duplicate callers, describe how your routing sends those repeat callers to a different network, and calculate the monthly revenue that recovery adds against your tracking platform cost.
fields.example: Duplicates run at least 5 percent and sometimes up to 25 percent of call flow across hundreds of verticals [Ringba — ojcbZuG798w @ 00:14:05]. Routing every duplicate to a different network gets paid twice for the same caller, and duplicate routing alone pays for the tracking platform [Ringba — AMwEMCOuhA0 @ 00:56:56]. At 1,000 monthly calls, that is 50-250 extra sellable calls.

fields.name: margin_math
fields.prompt: Write out the full unit economics of one call: buyer price, publisher payout, spread, rejected and duplicate calls, telecom cost, and buyer credit risk, then show how margin changes if you pay publishers on every call instead of qualified ones.
fields.example: A $35 affiliate payout against a $50-plus buyer price leaves a $15 spread, and 500 calls a day yields $7,500 daily [John Ventura — KeC4mKXnzs4 @ 00:03:05]. In TrackDrive's 100-call example, paying the publisher on all 100 instead of the 80 that qualify drops a 30 percent margin of $1,200 to 12.5 percent, or $500 [TrackDrive — yYZ5s6jFzQs @ 00:02:04].

fields.name: payment_terms
fields.prompt: Define the payment terms you will require from buyers and offer to publishers, including minimum deposits, prepayment versus credit, net terms alignment, and the review period before a new affiliate's calls become eligible for any payout at all.
fields.example: Buyers pay upfront with a $500 to $1,000 minimum deposit, and invoice insurance is reserved for massive deals [ceohec — SkS03nygdoY @ 00:08:10]. Net terms are aligned so buyer wires clear before publishers are paid, and new affiliates wait until their calls are reviewed, because paying too quickly invites fraud [Ringba — AMwEMCOuhA0 @ 01:13:11].

fields.name: qa_dispute_protocol
fields.prompt: Describe your quality assurance and dispute process, including the signed documents affiliates must return, the penalty for callback fraud, how disputes are written with dated specifics, and how you separate invalid calls from buyer closing problems.
fields.example: Affiliates sign a QA addendum carrying a 50 percent penalty per CPA for callback fraud [Ringba — JxU9bgFTUUs @ 00:20:34]. Disputes cite dates: 'between the third and the seventh' [TrackDrive — y8V08rKKNWY @ 00:04:31]. When 15 of 100 calls are disputed, the cause is investigated, since a buyer failing to close is not an invalid call [ExclusiveLiveCall — b7P50zcQzTs @ 00:07:01].

fields.name: scale_gate
fields.prompt: Set the exact thresholds that must be met before you add publishers or raise caps, including billable rate, post-reconciliation margin, and QA results, and state how many new affiliates you will onboard in any single step.
fields.example: Scale only at a billable rate of 50 percent or higher, positive post-reconciliation margin and clean QA, and never add 10 affiliates at once [John Ventura — KeC4mKXnzs4 @ 00:09:37]. Marketcall's debt funnel saw 25-35 percent of calls go billable past 90 seconds [Marketcall — Dq9KUpYUWsE @ 00:09:49], and exit pages add 5-10 percent revenue [Marketcall — Dq9KUpYUWsE @ 00:14:48].

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 6 is complete only when at least two networks are routing side by side with written concurrency figures, a direct-buyer pitch path is underway, the full unit economics of one call show a positive spread after rejects and duplicates, buyer deposits and aligned net terms are in place, a signed QA addendum covers every affiliate, and billable rate sits at or above 50 percent before any new publisher is added.
